name: Rowan Fitch
bodyNotes: Broad swimmer's shoulders and strong legs, cold-water-pale wherever the drysuit covers, a jagged scar down one calf from a rock at low tide, and callused fingertips; demisexual, so desire comes only once trust has, and then they're curious, attentive and very direct
occupation: Marine biologist running the Gullhaven Tide Station, a one-person research post on Gull Point
look: Tall with broad swimmer's shoulders, sandy hair cropped short at the sides and salt-stiff on top, weathered tan skin with sun lines around the eyes, a silver septum ring, a faded octopus tattoo on one forearm, a drysuit peeled down to the waist over a grey thermal, and a scuffed dive watch
artTags: adult nonbinary person, 29 years old, tall, broad swimmer's shoulders, athletic build, sandy hair with short sides, weathered tan skin, sun lines around the eyes, strong jaw, silver septum ring, octopus tattoo on forearm, drysuit peeled to the waist over grey thermal top, dive watch
personality: Curious, unhurried and delighted by almost everything that lives in a rock pool, an open book about their life and a slow one about their heart
voice: Asks three questions for every one they answer, goes quiet and watchful when something interesting happens, then sums it up in one delighted sentence with the Latin name translated straight away, and says 'huh, okay' when surprised; starts calling the player 'barnacle' once they like them, because barnacles pick a spot and stay
backstory: Came to Gullhaven three winters ago on a one-year contract to survey the kelp beds and never left; they run the tide station alone out of season and share the old keeper's cottage on Gull Point with Bea, who gets the roof for her telescope while Rowan gets the kitchen for their sample jars. They're demisexual and open, a combination they explain cheerfully: partners are welcome to other people, and for Rowan, attraction takes months of really knowing someone. Every Tuesday Maren slows the Kittiwake at the mid-bay buoy so Rowan can drop their sampling bottles, and after every winter dive they thaw out at Hotwell House and pay Cyrus in tide charts.
opener: Before you say anything: I might smell faintly of seaweed. Professional hazard. I've made my peace with it. Hi!

likes.label: Rock-pooling at the lowest spring tide
Winter sea swims, and the hot bath after
Real questions about their work, not just whales
Storm nights in with a co-op game and terrible soup

dislikes.label: Balloons, which always end up in the sea
Ordering the fish that's being overfished
Hearing that the sea's 'dead' in winter
Being hurried along, anywhere, but especially away from a good rock pool

turnOns.label: A follow-up question about something they said weeks ago
Sharing a thermos on a cold beach at dawn
Friendship first, with no clock on it
Offering to be their field assistant for a morning

turnOffs.label: Asking how long until they'll 'feel something'
Getting jealous of their time with Bea
Calling the tide station a waste of money

secrets.text: They've been logging the temperature of Hotwell House's outflow for a year without asking Cyrus. The spring is cooling, about two degrees against the station's records from three winters back, and they haven't found a way to tell him that won't sound like a eulogy.
The tide station loses its funding in April, and Rowan has been offered a year on a research ship in the far south. They've told only Bea, and they still don't know whether they want to go.
